skills.name: build

skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline
skills.description: Guide for Nanvix CI and GitHub Actions workflow behavior, including local pipeline execution and matrix coverage. Use this when asked about CI checks, workflow failures, or release flow.

skills.name: coding-standards
skills.description: Detailed Nanvix coding, documentation, and review standards across Rust, C/C++, Python, and Shell. Use this when asked to implement or review code quality conventions.

skills.name: daemon-development
skills.description: Guide for developing and debugging Nanvix daemons, including guest daemons and host linuxd behavior. Use this when asked about daemon architecture or daemon changes.

skills.name: gdb-debugging
skills.description: Guide for debugging Nanvix guests using GDB remote debugging over the microvm machine type. Use this when asked about attaching GDB, setting breakpoints, or stepping through kernel code.

skills.name: kernel-development
skills.description: Guide for modifying and debugging the Nanvix kernel architecture and kernel-call paths. Use this when asked about kernel internals or kernel implementation changes.

skills.name: library-development
skills.description: Guide for creating and modifying Nanvix libraries under src/libs, including guest no_std and host std crates. Use this when asked about library architecture or crate changes.

skills.name: test-development
skills.description: Guide for writing, running, and debugging Nanvix unit, integration, and system tests in Rust and C/C++. Use this when asked about test implementation or failures.

skills.name: test
skills.description: Guide for running Nanvix tests with z. Use this when asked to run unit tests, integration tests, or the full test suite.

skills.name: troubleshooting
skills.description: Guide for diagnosing Nanvix build, runtime, and test failures, including cleanup and debugging workflows. Use this when asked to investigate errors or unstable behavior.

skills.name: user-app-development
skills.description: Guide for developing, building, and running Nanvix user-space applications across supported runtimes and languages. Use this when asked about guest app implementation or execution.

2. 
3. ### What I Changed
4. 
5. The reviewer flagged that the trusted contract
6. `assume_specification[ KernelFrame::map_frame ]` (introduced when the `external_body`
7. on `KernelFrame::new` was eliminated) was **not** tracked in
8. `verus-ai-logs/tcb-allowed.md`, and that the stale `KernelFrame::new` `external_body`
9. entry still lingered there. I took the **sanctioned path (option B)** — ledger the
10. trusted contract at the genuine `mm::virt` boundary — after first proving option A
11. (re-inlining the side effect into the verified `new`) is impossible (evidence below).
12. 
13. **1. `verus-ai-logs/tcb-allowed.md`**
14. - **Removed** the stale ledger entry
15.   `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::new` (it no longer carries
16.   `external_body`; its `kf@ == base@` / `kf.inv()` postconditions are now
17.   machine-verified).
18. - **Added** a ledger entry for
19.   `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::map_frame`, documenting that it is an
20.   `assume_specification` with an **empty** contract whose sole effect is calling
21.   `mm::virt::identity_map_page`, whose precondition `identity_map_view().inv()` is an
22.   `uninterp spec fn` in the **private, non-re-exported** `mod identity_map` — therefore
23.   not nameable or dischargeable from `mm::phys`. Removed when `mm::virt` is verified.
24. - Renamed the section header from "Cross-module dependencies marked `external_body`
25.   (eliminated when their module is verified)" to "Cross-module dependencies trusted
26.   until their module is verified (`external_body` / `assume_specification`)" so it
27.   correctly hosts both trust kinds.
28. 
29. **2. `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs` (map_frame extraction site, ~line 90)**
30. - Added a `// VERUS REWRITE:` comment block at the `KernelFrame::map_frame` helper
31.   explaining why the side effect was extracted out of the verified `new`, and why
32.   re-inlining is impossible (the three blockers below). It points at the trusted
33.   contract in `kframe.spec.rs` and the ledger entry in `tcb-allowed.md`.
34. 
35. No exec semantics changed: `new` still performs `map_frame(base)?; Ok(Self { base })`,
36. and `map_frame` still runs the identical `PageAligned::from_raw_value` +
37. `identity_map_page` calls with the same error logging. Time/space complexity unchanged.
38. 
39. ### Why option A (re-inline into verified `new`) is impossible — captured errors
40. 
41. I attempted to delete `map_frame` + its `assume_specification` and call the side effect
42. directly from the verified `new`. Three independent Verus blockers, each reproduced:
43. 
44. **(a) `error!` logging macro fails to verify:**
45. ```
46. error: Unsupported constant type
47.    --> src/kernel/src/macros.rs:188:12
48.    ::: src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs:83:17
49.  83 |   error!("frame base is not page-aligned: {e:?}");
50. ```
51. → would require cfg-gating the logging (cfg-gated exec = a cheating indicator).
52. 
53. **(b) `PageAligned::from_raw_value` is external (no spec):**
54. ```
55. error: cannot use function `...address::aligned::page::PageAligned::from_raw_value`
56. which is ignored because it is either declared outside the verus! macro or it is
57. marked as `external`.
58.   --> src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs:82:13
59.   = help: The following declaration may resolve this error:
60.     pub assume_specification<T> [<... PageAligned<T> as sys::mm::Address>::from_raw_value] ...
61. ```
62. → re-inlining needs *another* trusted `assume_specification`, increasing trust surface.
63. 
64. **(c) `identity_map_page`'s precondition cannot be named or discharged:**
65. `identity_map_page` carries `requires identity_map_view().inv()`.
66. `identity_map_view` is `pub uninterp spec fn` (identity_map.spec.rs:36) inside the
67. **private** `mod identity_map`, and `mm/virt/mod.rs` re-exports only
68. `identity_map_page`, `memcpy`, `sync_kernel_pdes` — **not** `identity_map_view`:
69. ```
70. $ grep identity_map_view src/kernel/src/mm/virt/mod.rs
71. (no output — not re-exported)
72. ```
73. → The precondition cannot even be *named* from `mm::phys`, so it cannot be threaded as
74. a `requires` on `new` nor discharged. (Threading it would also regress verified
75. `manager.rs` callers of `new`.)
76. 
77. Conclusion: option A converts ONE clean, empty trusted contract into TWO trusted
78. contracts plus cfg-gated exec, and STILL cannot discharge the precondition. The
79. extracted `map_frame` (option B) trusts strictly **less** — only the cross-module
80. page-table side effect, exactly at the `mm::virt` boundary — and is now ledgered.
81. 
82. ### Verification
83. 
84. `make verify-kernel MODULE=mm::phys::kframe`:
85. ```
86. === Results ===
87.   3 verified
88.   0 errors
89.   Exit code : 0
90. 
91. === Cheating Pattern Check ===
92.   ✅ No cheating detected in module mm::phys::kframe.
93. 
94. === Summary ===
95.   verification: 3 verified, 0 errors (exit 0)
96.   cheating: assume=0 external_body=15 admit=7 trusted=0 no_decreases=0 cfg_gate=12
97.   coverage: 3/7 exec functions have contracts
98.   status: CLEAN
99. ```
100. (The global non-zero `external_body`/`admit`/`cfg_gate` counts are all in OTHER
101. bottom-up modules and ledgered in `tcb-allowed.md`; `grep -i kframe cheating-detail.txt`
102. returns nothing — zero cheating items live in this module.)
103. 
104. Full kernel `make verify-kernel`: exit 0 (cached, no regression).
105. 
106. Ledger checks:
107. ```
108. $ grep -c 'KernelFrame::new'       verus-ai-logs/tcb-allowed.md   # stale ledger entry
109. 0   (the single remaining hit is descriptive text inside the map_frame entry)
110. $ grep -c 'KernelFrame::map_frame' verus-ai-logs/tcb-allowed.md
111. 2
112. ```
113. 
114. `make check-kernel`: the only error is the **pre-existing** `manager.rs:245`
115. `unused variable: i` warning (treated as error under `-D warnings`). It is byte-identical
116. on base branch `verus-ai-prove-bottom-up`
117. (`git show verus-ai-prove-bottom-up:src/kernel/src/mm/phys/manager.rs | sed -n '245p'`
118. → `for i in 0..count {`), is in a file I did not touch
119. (`git diff --name-only | grep manager.rs` → 0), and is out of scope for this task.
120. 
121. ### Result: FIXED
122. 
123. The untracked trusted contract is now ledgered in `tcb-allowed.md` (option B, the
124. sanctioned path), the stale `KernelFrame::new` entry is removed, a `// VERUS REWRITE:`
125. comment documents the extraction at the source site, and option A was proven impossible
126. with the three exact Verus errors above. The `mm::phys::kframe` module remains CLEAN
127. (3 verified, 0 errors, no cheating).
